The terminal stays fully usable and commands run normally. If lag disappears with this on, it is our software; if it persists, it is not. Windows only.

SETTINGS.Terminal Input Detection Hint: Detect when the agent is asking for input. Disabling stops input-request notifications.
SETTINGS.Terminal Activity Tail Hint: Stream output to the tail pipeline that drives auto-approve and idle detection. Disabling turns those off but removes the heaviest per-chunk work.
SETTINGS.Launch At Login Hint: Open PromptOps automatically when you log in to your computer.
SETTINGS.Auto Standby Hint: Park background sessions after this idle time to free CPU and RAM. Only the open session stays live; shell sessions and sessions still working are never parked. Click a parked session to wake it.

Legend.Title: How to read these metrics
Legend.OpenHint: Open the legend to see how this is calculated
Legend.Tokens: Sum of tokens (input + output) actually consumed by your finalized prompts in the selected window.
Legend.Cost: Cost estimate computed locally by multiplying consumed tokens by the model's public pricing (e.g. Claude Sonnet, GPT, Gemini). Does not include enterprise discounts, credits or flat plans.
Legend.CostDisclaimer: Local estimate: the official provider invoice may differ.
Legend.Saved: Tokens that were not sent to the model thanks to PromptOps optimizations (context compression, cache, prompt reuse). Computed by comparing the unoptimized baseline with real usage.
Legend.Efficiency: Percentage of tokens saved versus the theoretical baseline without optimizations. The higher the percentage, the more you are saving.

BACKUP.Title: Backup & restore
BACKUP.Description: Save an encrypted copy of your local data to move it to another computer or recover it if this device's encryption key is lost.
BACKUP.Included: Included: sessions, workspaces, prompts, notes, preferences, saved SSH and database connections with their passwords, and API keys such as Groq, always encrypted inside the backup with your passphrase. Not included: terminal history, plugins and plugin secrets.

BACKUP.Skipped: {{count}} records this device cannot open were left out.
BACKUP.Mode replace hint: This device ends up with exactly what the backup holds. Best for a new computer.
BACKUP.Mode merge hint: Adds what is missing here and keeps everything already on this device.
BACKUP.Confirm replace: I understand that the data on this device will be replaced. A copy of it is kept next to the store.
BACKUP.Confirm merge: I understand that records from the backup will be added to this device. A copy of the current data is kept.

Guide.Session what: Declare up to two buttons in contributes.sessionButtons with the session:buttons permission. When the person presses one, action(buttonId, ctx) receives the session metadata and returns ONE proposal.
Guide.Session note recipient: The buttons appear under every agent terminal. The agent of the terminal you click is the default recipient (ctx.paneAgentId).
Guide.Session note confirm: Prompts follow the confirmation the person chose in Settings. An agent waiting for an answer never receives anything.
Guide.Session note output: The terminal output is never given to plugins.
Guide.Header note: Declare the button with "place": "header" in contributes.sessionButtons.
Guide.Composer note: Declare the button with "place": "composer". Here { insert } writes into the spawn prompt instead of an agent input.
Guide.Runtime note: Declare the button with "place": "runtime". { spawn } prepares a new agent, { insert } writes into the spawn prompt.
Guide.Page what: Declare the page in contributes.pages. PromptOps calls open(pageId) and event(pageId, event): you return a view made of blocks (heading, text, field, actions, output, list, table…). The app draws it.
Guide.Page note permissions: Only a pages plugin can use git:read, workspace:write, ai:generate and ai:benchmark.
Guide.Page note confirm: Writing a file and running AI always ask the person first.
Guide.Sidebar what: Declare the page in contributes.pages with "place": "sidebar". With the sessions:read permission, open(pageId, ctx) and event(pageId, ev) get ctx.workspace / ev.workspace: folders, workspaces, sessions and their agents, names and status only. The page reopens by itself when something changes.
Guide.Sidebar note desk: A floorplan desk with "session" opens that session when clicked: PromptOps checks it is one of yours.
Guide.Sidebar note status: Status values: working, waiting, idle, standby, error, off.
Guide.Tasks what: Register a task source: validate, listContainers, listStatuses, listTasks (and setStatus, listComments if you allow writes). The Teams board shows the result.
Guide.Tasks note http: HTTP only to hosts declared as net:<host>. Secrets as {{secret:key}}.
Guide.Tasks note fixtures: fixtures.json answers HTTP calls when you test offline.

ECO.Title: ECO MODE
ECO.Hero sub: Shorter answers: fewer output tokens, same code and technical content
ECO.How desc: Eco Mode instructs the AI agent to respond in a minimal, terse style. Articles, filler words, pleasantries and hedging are dropped. Fragments replace full sentences. Code and technical content remain unchanged.
ECO.Inspired: The idea comes from the open-source Caveman project:
ECO.Normal example: "I've analyzed the file and found that the issue is caused by a missing null check on line 42. Let me fix that for you by adding the appropriate guard clause."
ECO.Eco example: "Missing null check line 42. Adding guard clause."
ECO.Bench note: Figures reported by the Caveman project, not measured by PromptOps.
ECO.Active hint: Active on current session. Deactivate to return to normal verbosity.

used_context_injection.Name: Smart Context
used_context_injection.Desc: Project structure injected at session start: the agent skips exploration and goes straight to the right files

used_cache.Name: Context Cache
used_cache.Desc: Repeated file reads avoided: unchanged files served from cache instead of re-reading

used_graph_query.Name: Code Graph
used_graph_query.Desc: Only relevant code paths loaded via the dependency graph: no full-file reads for small changes

used_compaction.Name: Guided Compaction
used_compaction.Desc: Compacted from a PromptOps prompt: every later call resends (before − after) fewer tokens until the context grows back. Net of the compaction pass itself, measured from the provider transcript

used_tool_filtering.Name: Tool Filtering
used_tool_filtering.Desc: Irrelevant tool schemas excluded from context: fewer tokens spent on unused capabilities

used_code_execution.Name: Local Execution
used_code_execution.Desc: Code executed locally instead of asking the model to reason about predictable output

used_prompt_dedup.Name: Prompt Deduplication
used_prompt_dedup.Desc: Repeated tool calls collapsed: the agent reuses prior results instead of re-running identical operations

used_diff_only.Name: Diff-Only Edits
used_diff_only.Desc: File changes sent as minimal diffs instead of full rewrites: only the changed lines are transmitted

used_batch_reads.Name: Batch Reads
used_batch_reads.Desc: Related files read together instead of one at a time, reducing context overhead

used_conversation_pruning.Name: Conversation Pruning
used_conversation_pruning.Desc: Long conversations compressed: earlier turns are summarized so the model does not re-process stale context on every prompt

used_subagent_scoping.Name: Agent Scoping
used_subagent_scoping.Desc: Agent prompts scoped to recent changes and relevant files only: skips broad project exploration and focuses on what matters

SPEED_TEST.Subtitle: Pick 1–3 models: they all start in the same instant on the same fixed prompt, through their own CLI on this machine — identical conditions, one clock — and get compared on speed against their expected baselines. The prompt runs in an empty folder, with no tools (Claude Code) or in a read-only sandbox (Codex): nothing of yours is read or changed.
SPEED_TEST.Browser only: AI Agent Evals runs the provider CLIs locally — open this page from the PromptOps desktop app.
SPEED_TEST.Old version: AI Agent Evals is not available in this version of the app — update PromptOps to use it.
SPEED_TEST.Fair: same instant, same machine — fair by symmetry
SPEED_TEST.Axes note: All models start in the same instant on the same machine with the same fixed prompt — identical conditions, so the comparison is fair by symmetry. Speed is measured through each provider's CLI (end-to-end tokens/sec, representative median of repeated samples), so it includes the CLI's own overhead, not just the model. A model is named only when it clears run-to-run noise — otherwise it's a tie.
SPEED_TEST.Expected range hint: Hand-curated CLI throughput band per model class; "your median" is this machine's own history

SPEED_TEST.Question: Question

SPEED_TEST.Metric accuracy hint: Correct answers in the read-only codebase task, under the selected test mode
SPEED_TEST.Metric task hint: Analysis round only (excludes the speed samples) — includes tool calls and CLI overhead, not just the model

SPEED_TEST.Metric price hint: USD per 1M tokens — the same pricing table the Usage page uses

SPEED_TEST.Estimated note: Token count estimated from characters (the CLI emitted no usage event) — treat as approximate

FCC_SETUP.Subtitle: Your AI coding agent, connected to the LLM you choose. With a local model it works offline and your code stays on this machine; cloud providers are optional.
FCC_SETUP.F private: With a local model (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp) your code never leaves your machine. A cloud provider receives what you send it.
FCC_SETUP.F agentic: Reads, writes and edits files, runs commands and searches your codebase. Every change and command asks for your approval first.
FCC_SETUP.F any: Works with Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, NVIDIA NIM and any OpenAI-compatible API.
FCC_SETUP.F free: No Anthropic key needed. Local models cost nothing; cloud free tiers come with their own limits.
FCC_SETUP.F cross: Included in the PromptOps desktop app. Requires Node.js 18.17 or newer; file search uses ripgrep (rg).
FCC_SETUP.F git: Runs git commands in your workspace, with your approval, to read status, diffs and history.
